factProposals.value: Risk assessment takes a list of registered AI systems: the inventory fields (id, name, department, purpose, owner, status) plus four risk fields — dataCategories, decisionImpact, humanOversight and userFacing. Until the STORY-004 inventory exists it is supplied as JSON.

A risk assessment report per run: each assessed system with an overall rating (high, medium or low) and its risks, each with a category, severity, the rule that raised it, a plain-language reason and suggested mitigations; plus unassessed and failed systems and the report's limits.
Risks fall into six categories: privacy, fairness, human_oversight, transparency, security and accountability, with severities low, medium and high.
Only the compliance officer, security officer and operations manager roles may run or read a risk assessment; anyone else is refused and the refusal is logged.

A system with incomplete or invalid data is reported unassessed with each missing field named while the others are assessed; a risk model error marks that system failed and the run is not saved; a run past its time limit (default 30 s) or cancelled is interrupted, saves nothing and can be re-run.

Every risk assessment step (request, denial, start, each system assessed with its full result and mitigations, unassessed, failed, completed, interrupted, replayed) is written to the hash-chained audit log with the requesting user's id and a timestamp, before the result is saved or returned.

decisions.statement: Use a rule-based risk model behind a pluggable interface rather than calling Claude now.
decisions.rationale: No Claude risk-assessment skill or API key exists in the project; rules are explainable and testable offline, and a Claude-backed model can implement the same interface later. Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Assess systems with complete data and report incomplete ones as unassessed, rather than refusing the whole run.
decisions.rationale: One badly registered system should not block the assessment of the rest. Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Allow the compliance officer, security officer and operations manager roles to run risk assessments.
decisions.rationale: Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Check every risk model's output (known category and severity, a reason, at least one mitigation) and treat anything malformed as a model error, never as a finding.
decisions.rationale: A future model must not be able to report a risk without a category or a mitigation.

decisions.statement: Do not save an assessment where the model failed on any system, so a re-run with the same id retries it.
decisions.rationale: Saving it would replay the failure for ever under that id.

limitations.statement: The assessment is a rule-based first screen from registered details only; it does not inspect the systems, and a system rated low only means no rule fired.
No jurisdiction-specific law is applied; that is left to configurable governance controls (STORY-009).
Registered systems are passed in as JSON; there is no inventory store yet (STORY-004), and the system owner is a text field where the data model has owner_id.
The risk service is not yet wired into the STORY-001 orchestrator as a Risk Agent; the demo calls the service directly.
Identity is whatever the caller says it is; there is no login yet.
A timed-out model call is no longer waited for but is not forcibly stopped if it ignores the cancel signal.
